_comment: Alliances and rivalries (scripts/bonds.gd). Partners are NPC captains (a roster of named captains who sail the map, plus Nassau's council), officials, and nations (including the Brethren). Alliance levels 1-4, rivalry levels 1-3. need: the score a proposal must reach (their opinion of you, plus the parts listed in the acceptance breakdown). faction_need: your standing with a nation for each level. Benefits and costs are what the code does at each level; the texts here are what the player is told.

alliance.name: Understanding
alliance.text: You agree not to attack each other.

alliance.name: Pact
alliance.text: You share news and trade on better terms.

alliance.name: Alliance
alliance.text: You fight together, split plunder and answer each other's calls.

alliance.name: Sworn brotherhood
alliance.text: The deepest tie. Breaking it is never forgotten.

rivalry.name: Competition
rivalry.text: You race for the same prizes, contracts and markets.

rivalry.name: Feud
rivalry.text: Open hostility: they attack on sight and work against you ashore.

rivalry.name: Blood feud
rivalry.text: They will spend everything to destroy you, and you them.

captain: Their ship won't attack you, nor you theirs.
News of prizes and patrols; their friends think better of you.
Their ship joins your battles when it's near.
They come whenever you call, and back you in any council.
official: No more trouble from their office.
Better prices in their port and their best contracts.
A favour owed to you every month.
Their port never closes to you, and their group grows stronger.
faction: Their warships leave you be unless you're wanted.
Better prices in their ports; warships for sale sooner.
Their warships join your battles near their coasts.
Their ports never close to you. Their pardon is yours for nothing.

captain: Their rivals start to dislike you.
Their reputation rubs off on yours.
Calls for help, and a share of your plunder when they fight beside you.
Break it and every pirate in the Caribbean remembers.
official: Their rivals in office dislike you.
Rivals of theirs work against you.
They call in favours at bad moments.
Break it and every official hears.
faction: Their enemies' standing toward you drops.
The Brethren trust you less every month.
They expect you to fight their wars.
Pirates in your crew grow restless.
